The test image shows a strip/patch of completely dead, dried brown plants in a soybean field, surrounded by healthy green plants. Key observations:
- Clear patch of plant death in a row/strip pattern
- Brown, desiccated stems with leaf drop
- Surrounding plants appear healthy and green
- Dark moist soil visible

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome (patch death, leaf drop with petioles remaining), Phytophthora (patch death from stem rot), Soybean_Cyst_Nematode (patches of stunted/dead plants).

The reference image for Sudden Death Syndrome shows exactly the same field-level pattern: a distinct strip/row of dead, desiccated plants surrounded by healthy green soybeans. The top-left quadrant of the SDS reference is nearly identical to the test image — dead brown plants in a strip with healthy green canopy on both sides.

Additional supporting evidence:
- SDS causes patches/strips of plant death that appear suddenly
- The leaf drop pattern (leaflets fall, petioles may remain) matches the dried stems visible
- The dark moist soil conditions favor SDS development (wet conditions favor *Fusarium virguliforme*)
